newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's RCS Editori returns to profit in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Italy's RCS Editori returns to profit in 1996.

text.p: Italian publisher RCS Editori, until recently part of financial holding Gemina, returned to profit in 1996, making 1.5 billion lire versus a loss of 728.6 billion in 1995, its director general said.
RCS was included in the Gemina operations spun off into Holding Partecipazioni Industriali (HPI) formed earlier this year which is now due to merge with textile group Marzotto.
RCS Director General Claudio Calabi told a news conference the return to profit showed that "1996 was a year of change for the group, a return to normal thanks to intense effort on the costs front."
"RCS is substantially sorted out," Calabi said, adding its consolidated operating result was 50 billion lire with an improvement of 126.1 billion on 1995.
Net sales equalled 2.388 billion against 2.524 in 1995.
RCS, which had made a loss for three years in a row, had turned around due to a restructuring plan started in the second half of 1995.
Calabi stressed the value of RCS' accord with German group Burda, which took a 20 percent stake in RCS at the start of 1996 and which can be increased to 40 percent.
"Both groups consider this alliance strategic," he said.
RCS had reduced its net financial debt to 612.7 billion lire from 823.3 billion at the end of 1995, halving net financial charges to 48.3 billion due to capital operations in 1995.

For the first few months of 1997, operations were running in line with forecasts, with newspaper circulation better than expected, periodicals in line with targets despite difficult market conditions, and book publishing stable while advertising was feeling the effects of a weaker economy, he said.
